newsitem.title: UK: RTZ-CRA says won't change policy on hedging.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA says won't change policy on hedging.

text.p: Mining giant RTZ-CRA said it does not envisage any change to its policy on hedging, despite the impact of lower metal prices on its first-half results this year.
Chief executive Robert Wilson told a news briefing on Thursday that the company would have benefited from hedging its copper production over the past few months because prices had fallen so sharply.
"But that wouldn't induce us into a policy of hedging," Wilson said.
"If a company hedges sometimes and not others in a sense it takes a position as a speculator," he said.
If the company is operating in a market continuously the benefits of hedging are less, and can be very expensive, he explained.
Wilson said some U.S. copper producers had hedged output recently mainly through the use of put options, which effectively provide a floor price for their output.
But since most of these options were bought at around 90 cents a pound ($1,984/tonne), "they have only recently come into the money at all," Wilson said.
On Thursday copper was around two-month lows, with cash values indicated at $1,900.
The company says it is not normally active in short term commodity price or currency hedging programmes.

"Its normal policy is to sell its products at prevailing market prices. Exceptions to this rule are subject to strict limits laid down to the CRA and RTZ boards..." the company said in its 1995 annual report to shareholders.
The company maintains that a broad commodity and geographical spread help act against commodity price exposure.
